content.title: About
content.content: Fried green tomatoes are slices of unripe (green) tomatoes coated in flour, breadcrumbs or cornmeal and fried until golden and crisp. The dish is a staple of Southern U.S. cuisine and is often served as an appetizer or side.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally the tomatoes are harvested before they fully ripen, when they are firm and tart.
The dish gained popularity in the early 20th century thanks to restaurants in New Orleans and Jackson.
It is commonly served with a dipping sauce such as mayo‑ketchup blend or a classic “ranch” sauce.
Some regions use cornmeal instead of wheat flour for an extra crunchy crust.
Fried green tomatoes are a classic comfort‑food item that evokes nostalgia.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Green tomatoes contain lycopene and vitamin C, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in tomatoes promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: When fried with a modest amount of oil, they can be a relatively low‑calorie dish.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Frying adds calories and saturated fat, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes.

items.title: Salt and breadcrumbs
items.content: Excessive salt or processed breadcrumbs can contribute to high blood pressure.

items.title: Solanine in very unripe tomatoes
items.content: Extremely unripe tomatoes contain solanine, but normal culinary use keeps levels safe.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as an appetizer with remoulade, mayo‑ketchup sauce, or a spicy dip. They also make a tasty addition to sandwiches, burgers, or salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the oven to restore crispness.
